rootCause: The unpublished expansion's independent service oracle selected Azure Cosmos DB Restore / Vaulted Bckp Data Restore instead of the continuous-backup PITR restore meter. The existing engine already used the correct meter.

independentComparison.method: Fresh independent oracle API/math compared with a separately cached engine.

cases: Independent oracle selects PITR, not a conflicting vaulted-backup meter.
One-time per-GB restore is not multiplied by regions or running hours.
Both seven-day and thirty-day continuous backup restore charges are priced.
The original combined case preserves backup and all three analytical charges.
Zero restore quantity adds no restore line.
A missing PITR restore meter yields an explicit Cosmos pricing error and no partial component charge.

limitations: This resolves the expansion-branch service-oracle issue without merging unpublished Tier 1 service expansion into main or v1.4.
Live prices are time-bound. The deterministic fixture tests do not assert that a future regional API rate must remain unchanged.
The seven-day tier currently uses the same live restore meter as thirty-day retention; both are documented as charged per restore.
